content:
Reddit announces two upcoming changes that may upset some long-time users.

The company has already implemented one restriction on Old Reddit, and is now announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support is also being discontinued…

Old Reddit

Reddit underwent a major user interface overhaul back in 2018, which was strongly opposed by users who preferred the original version. In response to the feedback, the platform pledged at the time to keep "Old Reddit" accessible as long as people were still using it.

Back in August, the company began rolling out its first policy change, requiring Old Reddit users to be logged in. Now they're announcing that the legacy interface will only be available to users who have used it within the past six months, with new users being locked out.

Reddit says both changes are aimed at reducing AI scraping of the site's content (though if those companies are willing to pay, that apparently isn't a problem at all).

RSS Feeds Being Discontinued

The disabling of RSS feeds is being done for the same reason.

For some subreddits that rely on RSS for moderation work, this could cause significant problems. Reddit says it is aware of this and suggests moderators use Devvit apps like Discord Relay instead.

Users Aren't Happy

A look at the comments section makes it clear that many long-time users are very unhappy with the latest developments.

What do you think of these latest changes? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
